issues.legal_issue: The local planning authority is responsible for removing structures that contravene an operative town planning scheme, including structures on privately allotted plots.
material_facts: A final town planning scheme came into force and allotted final plots to private owners.
The scheme required huts and other temporary structures to be removed and provided for accommodation for people displaced by their removal.
Structures remained on the owners’ plots, and the local authority did not implement the scheme.
The owners sought removal only of structures that contravened the scheme or whose erection or construction failed to comply with it.
issues.conclusion: The local planning authority had the primary duty to remove the structures on the private plots to the extent that they contravened the scheme or were erected or carried out contrary to its provisions. The appeal was dismissed subject to limiting the removal order to those structures.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 51(3) of the Bombay Town Planning Act, 1954, a sanctioned final scheme has the effect of an enactment and is read as supplemental to the Act. Sections 53 and 54 provide for the determination of rights in final plots and summary eviction of persons occupying land contrary to those rights. Section 55(1)(a) authorises the local authority to remove, pull down or alter buildings or works anywhere in the scheme area that contravene the scheme; the Act places that responsibility on the authority, not the private plot owners. Note 11 of the scheme required the removal of the specified temporary structures, and the Act provided for displaced occupants. The corresponding provisions of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966, sections 88 to 90, were practically the same; section 165 continued the earlier schemes under the new Act.

predicates.town_planning_scheme_enforcement_case: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a final town planning scheme by the responsible planning authority.
predicates.final_scheme_in_force: A final town planning scheme governing the relevant area has come into force.
predicates.structures_contravene_scheme: Structures in the scheme area contravene the scheme or were erected or carried out without complying with its provisions.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks enforcement of an operative final town planning scheme and structures contravene it, the rule requires the planning authority to remove those structures.

issues.legal_issue: Receiving rent or compensation from occupants of structures does not, by itself, disqualify plot owners from obtaining mandamus to enforce a mandatory public duty.
material_facts: The owners sought mandamus requiring the local authority to implement the scheme and remove offending structures.
The owners or their predecessors had received amounts described as rent or compensation from hutment occupants.
The owners were not shown to be resisting enforcement of the scheme, and the local authority had failed to take effective action despite being called upon to do so.
The High Court exercised its discretion to grant relief.
issues.conclusion: The owners’ receipt of rent or compensation did not disqualify them from obtaining mandamus. The Court did not ordinarily interfere with the High Court’s exercise of discretion, and it found no adequate reason to refuse the writ.
issues.legal_principle: Mandamus may issue to require performance of a statutory duty where its performance is not discretionary. Although mandamus is discretionary, the Supreme Court ordinarily does not question a properly exercised discretion to grant it: The Queen v. The Church Wardens of All Saints, Wigan. The Queen v. Garland was distinguishable because relief there was refused on clean-hands grounds; no comparable disqualifying conduct was established here. The owners’ receipt of rent or compensation, without resistance to enforcement, did not amount to such disqualification.

rule.if: mandamus_proceeding and mandatory_public_duty and applicants_received_occupant_payments and applicants_not_resisting_enforcement

predicates.mandamus_proceeding: The applicants seek a writ requiring a public authority to perform a duty.
predicates.mandatory_public_duty: The authority is subject to a public duty whose performance is not discretionary.
predicates.applicants_received_occupant_payments: The applicants received rent or compensation from people occupying the relevant structures.
predicates.applicants_not_resisting_enforcement: The applicants are not shown to be obstructing enforcement of the applicable scheme.

issues.definition: When applicants seek mandamus to enforce a mandatory public duty, their receipt of occupant payments does not by itself disqualify them if they are not resisting enforcement.
